answer: An agent market handling ivory carvings and ferrous scrap at a wharf requires each identity to lock a $1,000 bond for 30 days before receiving a daily order quota. Splitting one agent into a thousand identities therefore requires $1 million in locked collateral; generating new keys alone earns no extra orders. The bond makes sybil capacity scale with committed capital, costing attackers liquidity and the returns that capital could earn elsewhere.
